I do not recommend buying EA games. Everything EA makes is garbage.
I purchased this game three years ago and never played it for a single minute. When I launched it for the first time today, I found that EA added the Javelin kernel-level anti-cheat in a later update, which enforces Secure Boot. Older machines are locked out and cannot launch the game. Many motherboards for 9th-generation Intel CPUs and earlier do not natively support Secure Boot. I spent a lot of time going through every option in the BIOS, but there is no solution at all.

Even if you have a new computer that meets the Secure Boot and TPM 2.0 requirements, do not think everything will be fine. This kernel-level anti-cheat has many problems: it easily causes blue screens and crashes, conflicts with various monitoring programs and peripheral drivers, carries a high risk of false positives, and imposes extremely strict background restrictions.

This mandatory requirement did not exist when I purchased the game. The developer unilaterally added this gameplay restriction afterward. You pay for the game, but whether you can play it is entirely up to the anti-cheat. Both new and old computers can run into problems.

This one-size-fits-all approach shows no respect for players’ genuine financial support. I will not buy any games produced by EA in the future.

就算你是满足安全启动、TPM2.0的新电脑也别觉得万事大吉，这套内核级反作弊毛病很多：容易蓝屏、死机、和各类监控、外设驱动冲突，误判风险高，后台限制极多。

Battlefield 2042 sells out franchise tradition for cheap gimmicks.

If you are thinking of picking up Battlefield 2042, think twice. It is a deeply disappointing entry that completely abandons key series staples, offering a thin, unpolished package that fails to justify its full asking price.

Here is why you should stay away from this installment:

• No Campaign or Narrative Anchor: In a lazy design shift, DICE opted to forego a single-player story campaign entirely to focus exclusively on multiplayer. Without a narrative mode to add value, teach mechanics, or anchor the experience, the severe lack of core content becomes painfully obvious the moment you launch the game.

• Extinct Game Modes: Matchmaking is a complete ghost town for anything outside of standard play. While you can find region-based matches for basic Conquest and Team Deathmatch, the rest of the game is effectively dead. The heavily marketed Hazard Zone mode has been completely abandoned, and the lack of meaningful post-launch content updates means the few active modes get boring fast.

• Cheap, Free-to-Play UI: The user interface and HUD feel shockingly unpolished and low-quality. Instead of looking like a premium, triple-A military shooter, the menus and in-game displays look like they were ripped straight out of a cheap, generic free-to-play mobile title.

• Aggressive Microtransactions: Progression feels hollow and unrewarding. Instead of earning cool unlocks through gameplay milestones or traditional reward crates, the progression system has been gutted to push microtransactions. The game constantly pesters you to spend real money on paid operator bundles and weapon skins.

Final Verdict: As a daily shooter, this title falls completely flat and cannot be recommended over superior options on the market. If you are absolutely determined to try it, do not pay full price—put it on your wishlist and wait for a steep discount.
